analysis: The PR changes two documentation lines only. docs/architecture/hardware-support.md line 121 adds a caveat: the gpt-oss-20b 3.5 GiB activation floor was measured with float32 activations after layer 0 and has not been re-measured with bf16 activations. docs/architecture/inference.md line 1620 adds a note that a bf16 gpt_oss checkpoint keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, because the expert SwiGLU clamp bounds take the activation dtype. No code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization or cache-crypto behavior changes, so I found no regression against TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, A-001, A-003, A-015, A-016, T-041 or the other listed definitions. T-041 (prefix cache) is untouched: the changed rows do not alter HMAC lookup names, TTL, disk budget or cacheSalt scoping. The added caveat is a documentation admission that the activation floor may be mismatched with the current bf16 path. If the floor is too low, the availability and memory-pressure risk is for the provider (T-029-style resource exhaustion and OOM). That is a calibration question, not a demonstrated security regression. The source files named (GPTOSS+Experts.swift, UnifiedMemoryCap.swift) are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify the doc claims about swiglu dtype or the floor's adequacy. A later pass could check whether the floor still covers bf16 gpt-oss-20b under the admission checks. The post-load KV headroom probe and the ledger-based admission remain the authoritative controls.
